history.summary: When a purple worm digests a dropped cockatrice corpse while the hero is swallowed, C petrifies the worm and constructs its statue. JavaScript reaches the same monstone path but supplies object creation with an rn2-only random override; obj.js rejects the incomplete provider before mksobj_at can finish. Repair mon.c:monstone's default random environment while preserving explicit injected providers and the source call order.

source.branch: After do.c:engulfer_digests_food identifies a swallowed cockatrice corpse and calls minstapetrify(u.ustuck, TRUE), the nonresistant purple worm reaches xkilled with gs.stoned set. xkilled calls monstone; because the purple worm is larger than tiny, monstone takes the statue branch, constructs the statue with mkcorpstat, and object initialization consumes C's global random stream.
callers: C do.c:dropz -> engulfer_digests_food -> trap.c:minstapetrify -> mon.c:xkilled -> monstone. JS js/do.js:dropz -> engulfer_digests_food calls js/trap.js:minstapetrify; its byplayer path calls js/mon.js:xkilled, which calls monstone when state.gs.stoned is true.

C mon.c:monstone calls mkobj.c:mkcorpstat for the statue, which calls mksobj_at and mksobj. JS mon.js:monstone passes objectGenerationEnv({ ...env, state, random }) to js/corpstat.js:mkcorpstat; mkcorpstat forwards it to js/obj.js:mksobj_at.
dependencies: mkobj.c:mkcorpstat and mksobj_at use C's global random functions during statue creation. Their existing JS implementations validate an injected provider in obj.js:sourceRandom; verify this contract, but do not claim or edit those source functions.

A private C/JS differential using the independent recipe reproduced that runtime exception. The differential cannot establish a matching prefix because runSegment throws before returning its captured output. A direct runSegment trace locates the throw at js/obj.js:sourceRandom, called by mksobj_at -> mkcorpstat -> monstone -> xkilled -> minstapetrify -> engulfer_digests_food -> dropz.

C mon.c:monstone (3287-3374) uses global rn2 for its own branch and calls mkcorpstat without a random argument; mkobj.c:mkcorpstat (2067 onward) calls mksobj_at, whose implementation calls mksobj. JavaScript mon.js:monstone defaults its local random provider to { rn2 } and passes that partial object through objectGenerationEnv to mkcorpstat, where obj.js:sourceRandom requires rn2, rnd, rn1, and rne. This is the source divergence; the existing monstone completion record covers the function generally but did not cover this omitted-provider path.
